> **Session focus:** *LISA collaborative attitude, co-authorship norms, role-play practice, and meeting structure*

## Learning Objectives

* Practice the LISA Collaborative Attitude in real scenarios
* Strengthen relationship-building behaviors and meeting structure
* Understand co-authorship principles and ethical collaboration norms
* Apply analogies and plain-language explanations in role-plays

## Description of Activities

On 20 May (Block 1), we focused on the LISA collaborative attitude, structured meetings (POWER), co-authorship practices, and applied communication via role-plays. Materials included checklists, analogies, and prompts to turn technical ideas into shared understanding.

## Reflection (Gibbs Reflective Cycle)

### 1. Description

We operationalized the LISA attitude—service-oriented, respectful, and empowering—through structured meetings and role-plays. We reviewed co-authorship norms and used analogies to translate complex ideas into shared language.

### 2. Feelings

I felt grounded by the clarity of behavioral cues (how to show respect, curiosity, and care). Discussing co-authorship reduced ambiguity I’ve felt around credit and accountability. Role-play was uncomfortable at first, then freeing as muscle memory formed.

### 3. Evaluation

The combination of attitude, structure, and practice worked. The LISA lens made small behaviors matter (greetings, agenda co-creation, follow-through). Co-authorship guidance was actionable—memos at project start prevent later conflict. Analogies improved clarity without losing rigor.

### 4. Analysis

ASCCR connects here: Attitude and Relationship are not soft extras; they are the context that makes Content persuasive and Communication effective. Mezirow’s lens surfaced my assumption that “writing authorship later is harmless”—a risky belief. Double-loop learning prompts me to address roles early as part of Structure.

### 5. Conclusion

Relationship-first doesn’t mean method-second; it means method-with-purpose. Clear roles and collaborative behaviors reduce friction and raise trust, enabling better science.

### 6. Action Plan

I will implement a standard opening (greeting, purpose, agenda, time), use a brief authorship/roles memo for new projects, and maintain an analogies bank for recurring explanations. I’ll request explicit feedback on how my behaviors support a collaborative atmosphere.
